body.translated_text: <s>Prajñāpāramitā-hṛdaya-sūtra</s> (The Heart Sūtra of the Perfection of Wisdom)
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to the Blessed Noble <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom)!

body.text:
Ārya Āvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo gambhīraṃ
prajñāpāramitā-cāryāṃ caramāṇo
vyavalokayati sma, pañca-skandhās tāṃś ca
svabhāva-śūnyān paśyati sma.
body.translated_text: The Noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, while practicing the profound <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom), looked down and beheld the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), and saw them to be empty of intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva-śūnya</s>).

body.text:
Iha Śāriputra rūpaṃ śūnyatā, śūnyat'aiva rūpaṃ,
rūpān na pṛthak śūnyatā,
śūnyatāyā na pṛthag rūpaṃ,
yad rūpaṃ sā śūnyatā,
yā śūnyatā tad rūpaṃ.
Evam eva vedanā-saṃjñā-saṃskārā-vijñānam.
body.translated_text: Here, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, form is emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), and emptiness itself is form; form is not different from emptiness, emptiness is not different from form; that which is form is emptiness, that which is emptiness is form. Likewise are feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), mental formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>), and consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>).

body.text:
Iha Śāriputra sarva-dharmāḥ śūnyatā-lakṣaṇā
anutpannā aniruddhā amalā avimalā anūnā aparipūrṇāḥ.
Tasmāc Chāriputra śūnyatāyāṃ na rūpaṃ
na vedanā na saṃjñā na saṃskārāḥ na vijñānaṃ,
na cakṣuḥ-śrotra-ghrāṇa-jihvā-kāya-manāṃsi,
na rūpa-śabda-gandha-rasa-spraṣṭavya-dharmāḥ,
na cakṣur-dhātur yāvan na mano-vijñāna-dhātuḥ,
n'āvidyā n'āvidyā-kṣayo yāvan na jarā-maraṇaṃ
na jarā-maraṇa-kṣayo na duḥkha-samudaya-nirodha-mārgā
na jñānaṃ na prāptir n'āprāptiḥ.
body.translated_text: Here, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) are marked by emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>): they are neither produced nor destroyed, neither defiled nor pure, neither deficient nor complete. Therefore, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, in emptiness there is no form, no feeling, no perception, no mental formations, no consciousness; no eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind; no form, sound, smell, taste, touch, or mental objects; no eye-element (<s>cakṣur-dhātu</s>) up to no mind-consciousness element (<s>mano-vijñāna-dhātu</s>); no ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) and no extinction of ignorance, up to no aging-and-death (<s>jarā-maraṇa</s>) and no extinction of aging-and-death; no suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), origination (<s>samudaya</s>), cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), or path (<s>mārga</s>); no knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), no attainment, and no non-attainment.

body.text:
Tasmāc Chāriputra aprāptitvād bodhisattvo
prajñā-pāramitām āśritya viharaty acitt'āvaraṇaḥ.
Citt'āvaraṇa-nāstitvād atrasto
viparyās'ātikrānto niṣṭhā-nirvāṇaḥ.
Tradhva-vyavasthitāḥ sarva-buddhāḥ
prajñāpāramitām āśritya anuttarāṃ
samyak-sambodhim abhisambuddhāḥ.
body.translated_text: Therefore, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, because there is no attainment, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, relying on <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom), dwells with no obstruction of mind. Because there is no obstruction of mind, there is no fear, and having transcended all error, one reaches final <s>Nirvāṇa</s> (liberation). All <s>Buddhas</s> abiding in the three times, relying on <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, have fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, complete enlightenment (<s>anuttarā samyak-saṃbodhi</s>).

body.text:
Tasmāj jñātavyaṃ prajñāpāramitā mahā-mantro
mahā-vidyā-mantro'nuttara-mantro
samasama-mantraḥ sarva-duḥkha-praśamanaḥ satyam amithyatvāt.
Prajñāpāramitāyām ukto mantraḥ, tadyathā -
Oṃ gate gate pāragate pārasaṃgate bodhi svāhā.
body.translated_text: Therefore, it should be known that <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is the great <s>mantra</s>, the <s>mantra</s> of great knowledge, the unsurpassed <s>mantra</s>, the <s>mantra</s> equal to the unequaled, which pacifies all suffering — it is true, because it is not false. In the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> this <s>mantra</s> is proclaimed, namely: <s>Oṃ gate gate pāragate pārasaṃgate bodhi svāhā</s> (Gone, gone, gone beyond, gone completely beyond — enlightenment, hail!).
Thus concludes the Noble <s>Prajñāpāramitā-hṛdaya</s> (Heart of the Perfection of Wisdom).
